hypothesis: A spinoff can trade below value in its first months when holders sell for reasons unrelated to value. This is a screen to prioritize filing review, not a recommendation or a validated return forecast.

factors.name: small relative to parent
factors.chapter: Greenblatt (1997), Chapter 3, on spinoffs; Klarman (1991), Chapter 10, pages on spinoffs
factors.definition: New company's market value divided by the parent's market value at distribution. Lower is better because the parent holders can be less likely to keep a small unwanted position.

factors.name: weakness in first weeks
factors.chapter: Greenblatt (1997), Chapter 3, on spinoffs; Klarman (1991), Chapter 10, pages on spinoffs
factors.definition: Return from the first official close after distribution through the screen price date. Lower is better because forced or indifferent selling can still be under way.

factors.name: few analysts
factors.definition: Count of named sell-side analysts or firms identified in a declared source on the screen date. Lower is better because the new company can have less initial coverage.

factors.name: insiders buying
factors.definition: Count of Form 4 open-market or private purchases with transaction code P after distribution. Higher is better.

factors.name: small absolute size
factors.chapter: Greenblatt (1997), Chapter 3, on spinoffs; Klarman (1991), Chapter 10, pages on spinoffs
factors.definition: New company's market value on the screen price date. Lower is better because a small issue can be outside the mandate of some holders.
